What if you could turn a 4-hour GTA 6 livestream into multiple ready-to-post YouTube Shorts without watching the entire stream?

That's exactly what this AI-powered GTA 6 Clipper does.

Just paste a YouTube, Twitch, or Kick stream link — or let the AI discover the biggest GTA 6 livestreams happening today. It automatically finds the most exciting moments and turns them into vertical videos with facecam, gameplay, animated captions, catchy hooks, and social media descriptions.

And the best part? You can build this entire workflow for free!

The system follows 4 simple steps:

1. Downloads Stream Audio

Instead of downloading an entire 4-hour livestream, it extracts only the audio, saving time and storage.

2. Analyses the Entire Stream

AI processes the audio locally and identifies:
- Full video transcripts
- Exciting or loud reactions
- Funny moments and unexpected discoveries
- Chat activity spikes on YouTube replays

3. Finds the Most Viral Moments

AI analyses the transcript in 12-minute sections and looks for moments people would actually want to share.

It identifies:
- First reactions
- Crazy GTA 6 discoveries
- Funny fails
- Streamer freakouts
- Unexpected moments
- Interesting opinions and hot takes

Every moment gets a score, and clips that need too much context are automatically rejected.

4. Automatically Creates Shorts

The system downloads only the relevant video sections and creates:
- Vertical 9:16 videos
- Facecam on top
- GTA 6 gameplay below
- Hook-based titles
- Word-by-word captions
- Social media descriptions
- Relevant hashtags

Here's what happened when I tested it on a real livestream:

- Stream duration: 30 minutes
- Potential moments discovered: 15
- Best moments selected: 3
- Processing time: 13 minutes 48 seconds

By default, it generates 3 clips per stream.

You can also process multiple livestreams simultaneously. For example, 7 streams could generate approximately 21 clips.

snippet.description:
🚀 Final Phase (the video editors and caption styles, all 23 of our skills in 1 platform): https://www.skool.com/finalphaseai/about
I built a clipper that turns a GTA 6 stream into vertical clips that are ready to post, and on launch day it can clip a stream while it's still live.

🆓 Our free Skool (the clipper, over 50 packs from my videos, over 23,000 people): https://www.skool.com/nextphase-5790
Already in Final Phase? The editors are already in the platform.
Weekly calls if you get stuck installing anything.

The real run: three GTA 6 Extended Look reaction streams at once, from CaseOh, MoistCr1TiKaL and Jynxzi. That's five and a half hours of stream. It listened to all of it in about eight minutes, found 34 moments worth a look and kept nine, three per stream. From pasting three links to nine clips ready to post took about 30 minutes, and I didn't touch anything in between.

What the clipper does
1. You give it a link from YouTube, Twitch or Kick, or it finds today's biggest GTA 6 streams by itself.
2. It downloads only the audio (a four-hour stream is a few hundred megabytes) and transcribes it on your computer, marking where the streamer laughed, screamed or got louder than their normal.
3. It reads the room: how fast chat moves compared to normal, what chat types ("CLIP IT", "LMAO", walls of question marks), YouTube's most-replayed graph, and the clips Twitch viewers already made, down to the second. All of it goes into one hype curve.
4. The AI reads the transcript 12 minutes at a time and scores every moment, harshly. The best ones go head to head in a final round: would a stranger stop scrolling in two seconds, does it make sense with zero context, does it pay off inside the clip.
5. It never clips the same moment twice, and it warns you when there's a copyrighted song under a clip.
6. It downloads only the minutes it needs, finds the facecam, picks the layout scene by scene, cuts the dead air, adds a hook title and word-by-word captions and sets the volume where Shorts want it.
7. Every clip checks itself (length, loudness, black frames, the face), gets a caption with hashtags, and lands on a page where you can watch them all and copy each caption.

Live mode: say "clip this live stream" and paste the link. It records in the background, listens every 20 seconds, and when chat explodes it shows Claude the last minute. A yes is a finished clip on your computer about three minutes after it happened.

Two ways to run it
Way 1: your Claude subscription (Pro is $20 a month billed monthly, or $17 a month billed yearly, US prices on claude.com/pricing). Everything except the picking runs on your computer for free, no API keys. Put the clipper in your Claude skills folder (or drag the folder into Claude Code) and say "set up the clipper".
Way 2: free. Install Ollama and Claude Code, download a model that fits your memory (16 GB: Qwen 3.5 9B, 32 GB or more: Qwen 3.5 27B), then run "ollama launch claude". The free model is slower and its picks are rougher; everything else runs the same.

Before you post
YouTube pays Shorts through the YouTube Partner Program: 1,000 subscribers and 10 million valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days. It can turn down channels that only repost, so add something of your own. Clip streamers who are fine with clipping, and watch every clip before you post it.

Credits
Stream footage shown for commentary: MoreCaseOh, MoistCr1TiKaL Gaming and Jynxzi on YouTube. The GTA VI trailer playing inside their streams belongs to Rockstar Games. Real chat replay from MoistCr1TiKaL Gaming's stream. The crowd-clip example uses clips viewers made of TimTheTatman's Twitch VOD. Pages shown: skool.com, contentrewards.com, claude.com, ollama.com, support.google.com. Not affiliated with any of them. This video is not sponsored.
